channel.title: fieldnotes
channel.description: Writing and evidence: agent systems, models, evaluation and computational biology.

item.title: Which model holds the seat, and what to do when it does not
item.description: A leaderboard averages over the wrong axis. What matters is which model wins which seat, on what evidence, and which rung of the intervention ladder a failure points at.

item.title: Memory management for LLM-on-corpus
item.description: Parametric state, chain-of-thought, flat RAG and graph-RAG are four answers to the same question, and the partitioning algorithm separates the principled tools from the rest.

item.title: 6.6W versus 35W, and a desk-scale PUE argument
item.description: Sustained eval workloads are watts-bound on a desk-scale box, and the fan moving air through a hot chassis is a bigger share of that than it looks.

item.title: Why I Started Building a Local Multi-Model Workforce, and Why the Industry May Be Heading There Too
item.description: How a self-directed effort grew into a supervised multi-model architecture, a set of working products, and an emerging professional direction.

item.title: Building a 4B Local Implementer
item.description: The task-bound Implementer, its behavioural adaptation, repeated coding evaluation, evidence flywheel and next steps.

item.title: Building a 4B Local Implementer: technical report
item.description: Training regime, paired evaluation across fifteen HumanEval+ runs, and what the numbers do and do not support.

item.title: A reasoning manual helped a small model catch the trap
item.description: On granite-4.0-h-small-FP8 the manual raised the catch rate from 8/24 to 16/24, while a same-length placebo did nothing. Small n, stated plainly.

item.title: The prompt is not the model
item.description: Seven models over 184 output-prediction problems. The headline change is meaningless on its own, the effect is bimodal, and the real signal is the floor.

item.title: The gate opened, and the manual still moved nothing
item.description: A weaker base model and a harder trap gave the manual room to show a capability effect. It did not.

item.title: Seven local models on output prediction
item.description: 100 Python problems, graded strictly at Pass@1 and reported together with its prompt, infrastructure and harness failures.

item.title: The manual moved only the labels
item.description: Three arms, three tiers and twenty-seven agents, with a sham arm so a real capability effect would have had room to appear.

item.title: It changed how the work was shown, not what was caught
item.description: Nine traps, model held constant, one arm reading the operating manual and one not.
